cards.explanation: The answer is justice. Micah, a prophet of the LORD, asks the leaders, "Should you not know justice?" (Micah 3:1). Look at who he's asking: the rulers, the very ones in charge. If I ran a bakery and didn't know what an oven was, I'd have bigger problems than a blurry stamp. Those in charge are the ones you'd expect to know it best.

The answer is False. Micah says the reverse: the leaders "…hate good and love evil." (Micah 3:2). He's speaking to the people who are supposed to guard what's right. Instead, the text says they've got the two backwards.

The answer is that He will not answer them. Micah says, "Then they will cry out to the LORD, but He will not answer them." (Micah 3:4). It's a heavy line, and it comes right after the harm he described in the verses before. The text says plainly that the answer will be silence.

The answer is True, and the text gives the reason. Micah says, "At that time He will hide His face from them because of the evil they have done." (Micah 3:4). It's the same stretch of verses where he said they hate good and love evil. The reason comes straight from the verse.

The answer is war. The LORD says these prophets "…declare war against one who puts nothing in their mouths…" (Micah 3:5). They proclaim peace while they chew, and the war goes to the one who gives them nothing. I've been in kitchens with more honest signals than that.

The answer is False. No honor is handed out to the seers and diviners. Micah says, "Then the seers will be ashamed and the diviners will be disgraced." (Micah 3:7). That comes after night falls over them without visions (Micah 3:6). Shame and disgrace are what the text gives them.

The answer is that there is no answer from God. The verse gives the reason itself. The seers and diviners "…will all cover their mouths because there is no answer from God." (Micah 3:7). A seer with nothing to see has nothing left to say. You know when everybody in the meeting turns to you for the answer and you've got NOTHING? That's the hand over the mouth.

The answer is the Spirit of the LORD. Micah says, "…I am filled with power by the Spirit of the LORD, with justice and courage…" (Micah 3:8). That's the 'however' after all the silence in the verses before. The seers will have no answer from God, and Micah has the Spirit of the LORD. His power comes from there, not from his own muscles, which in my case would be a relief.

The answer is their transgression and sin. Micah says he's filled "…to declare to Jacob his transgression and to Israel his sin." (Micah 3:8). That's a tough message to deliver, and it takes courage to say it. The text names what he declares: transgression and sin.

The answer is bloodshed and iniquity. Micah says they are the ones "…who build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with iniquity." (Micah 3:10). The building materials are the problem. That's a shaky foundation, friends.

The answer is True. Micah says, "…her priests teach for a price…" (Micah 3:11). Teaching, with a price tag stuck right on it. It's there in his list with the leaders and the prophets. He names all three.

The answer is that the LORD is among them, so no disaster can come. They say, "Is not the LORD among us? No disaster can come upon us." (Micah 3:11). Notice that Micah says they lean upon the LORD even as they judge for a bribe and teach for a price. Bribes and all, and they STILL say no disaster can come. Micah's very next words say otherwise.

The answer is that Zion will be plowed like a field. Micah says, "Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field…" (Micah 3:12). He pictures Zion plowed like a field. I think that's a hard picture to take in. Micah says it's because of them.

The answer is False. The temple mount isn't spared. Micah says, "…Jerusalem will become a heap of rubble, and the temple mount a wooded ridge." (Micah 3:12). Even the mount where the temple stands is named. That's a sobering line, and the text doesn't soften it.
